title: Listening Section 3 - Presentation Preparation Tutorial
instruction: You will hear a student, Aisha, talking to her tutor, Dr Evans, about a history presentation. Answer Questions 1-10.

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: Come in, Aisha. You wanted to talk about your presentation on the Silk Road?

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: Yes, Dr Evans. I'm worried it's too long. I planned fifteen minutes, but I have a lot of material.

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: The limit for this assignment is twelve minutes, so you will need to cut some. Thirteen would lose you marks.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: Twelve. All right. I also have a lot of slides. Is there a limit?

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: No more than ten, I'd say. Otherwise, you'll rush. What are your main sections?

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: I start with the history of silk production, then the main trade goods, which were silk, spices and paper. After that I have a section on modern tourism along the route, and finally a conclusion.

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: I'd cut the section on modern tourism. It's interesting, but it doesn't answer the question you were set. And for the introduction, try a map. It shows the audience the whole route at a glance, which a quotation or a video wouldn't do.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: Good idea. Should I discuss one city in detail?

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: Yes, a case study works well. Samarkand would be a good choice. Do you know how to spell it?

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: Correct. What about your notes? Last time I noticed you read straight from them.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: I know. I get nervous and I don't want to forget anything.

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: Write only key words on cards. And practise by recording yourself on your phone, then listen to it. You'll notice where you speed up.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: I'll try that. When is the presentation again?

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: It's on Thursday, in room 12. You'll have five minutes for questions at the end.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: Is there anything I should read before then?

transcript.speaker: Evans
transcript.text: I'll email you a couple of useful articles this afternoon. Don't try to read too much, though. Focus on rehearsing.

transcript.speaker: Aisha
transcript.text: Thank you, Dr Evans. That's really helpful.

options.optionText: A. the history of silk production
